title: The Papers: 'Brexit and Thatcher to blame' and 'Hottest summer ever'
originalTitle: The Papers: 'Brexit and Thatcher to blame' and 'Hottest summer ever'
content:
Most of the papers focus on Andy Burnham's first appearance in the Commons as Prime Minister on Tuesday.

The Daily Mail, external calls him a "messiah without a mandate" -- and says that since he blamed the country's problems on "Thatcher and Brexit", it's no wonder the Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, mocked the prime minister for "living in the past". And the Daily Express, external agrees, warning that Burnham wants to take Britain "back to the 70s".

"Fresh start versus Farage farce" is the headline in the Daily Mirror, external. It leads with a combination of Burnham promising to make the next decade better than the last, and Farage being sworn in on his return to Parliament after the Clacton by-election.

The financial markets have "turned on" Burnham, according to the Daily Telegraph, external - which says a market "rout" overshadowed his address to MPs. The Financial Times, external says with government borrowing costs now the highest since the 2008 financial crisis, pressure has been piled on the prime minister and chancellor ahead of this autumn's budget.

Elsewhere, the Times, external reports that police did not tell the families of the victims of the Nottingham attacks that they were being stalked by a mentally ill man. The paper says he travelled to Somerset to find the parents of Barnaby Webber, and attended a GP surgery where Grace O'Malley-Kumar's father worked. Nottinghamshire Police has referred itself to the police watchdog, and said it could not comment during the investigation.

The i Paper, external picks up on a report from the US that scientists could have found dark matter on Earth for the first time. It says a team in South Dakota, using a tank of liquid xenon buried a mile underground, might have detected a "Wimp" - a weakly interacting massive particle - that's thought to be the key to dark matter.

Ever fancied getting a better look at your teeth while you brush them? Well now you can, according to the Guardian, external. It reviews Dyson's latest toothbrush - which will offer you a livestream of the inside of your mouth while you clean. But the paper warns that will come at a cost - £419 to be precise.
